post.titulo: Everyday English Conversation Practice | A2 English Podcast | Ep. 1 — Mia's Busy Day
post.descricao:
Everyday English Conversation Practice for A2 learners: follow Mia's busy day and speak real English with easy, slow conversations.

In this episode you will learn:
- 5 everyday expressions: How's it going? · I just moved here. · I'd like... · How do I get to...? · Sounds good!
- 3 common mistakes and how to fix them: people is/are · said me/told me · How much costs it?
- 10 sentences to repeat out loud (shadowing)
- The coffee shop scene again at natural speed
- Quiz: what is wrong with "I lost the bus"? (answer at the end)

Real-life situations: greeting a neighbor, ordering coffee, asking for directions, taking the bus, small talk at work, the supermarket checkout and making plans on the phone.

Tell us in the comments: what did you do this morning? Use one expression from today.

Mia and Leo are fictional characters.
Voices are AI-generated; story and lessons written and reviewed by our team.

falas.texto: Leo! Leo! You won't believe my day. This morning, I lost the bus!
You lost the bus? Wow. It's very big. Did you check under your bed?
Very funny. You know what I mean.
I do. But one word is wrong. That's today's quiz.

card.pergunta: "This morning, I lost the bus." What should Mia say?

falas.texto: What should Mia say? Think about it. The answer comes at the end.
Hi, everyone, and welcome to the English Mistake Fix Podcast. I'm Leo. I'm your teacher, and I fix mistakes. Gently.
And I'm Mia. I make the mistakes. A lot of mistakes.
That's why we're a good team. This is our Easy series, level A2. Today's topic is everyday English conversations.
Small, normal conversations. Like with a neighbor, or at a coffee shop, or on the bus.
Exactly. Today you will learn three things.

itens: 3 common mistakes and how to fix them

falas.texto: One. Five everyday expressions. Two. Three common mistakes, and how to fix them. Three. Ten useful sentences. You will say them out loud with us.
So get your coffee, or your tea, and relax.
Tea for me. Always tea. My cat, Biscuit, is already asleep on my keyboard. So let's start before he wakes up.
Biscuit never wakes up, Leo.
True. He is a very lazy cat. Okay, Mia. You just moved to a new city, right?
Yes! Two weeks ago. New city, new apartment, new job. Everything is new.
Then tell us about your day. From the beginning. And I will play the other people in your story.
Great. So, it was seven thirty in the morning. I opened my door, and...
Okay. I'll be your neighbor. An older man with a small dog. Ready?
Ready.
Good morning! How's it going?
Oh! Good morning! It's going well, thanks. And you?
Not bad, not bad. I'm Frank. I live next door, in apartment four. Are you new here?
Yes. I just moved here. Two weeks ago. My name is Mia.
Nice to meet you, Mia. Welcome to the building. Do you like the neighborhood?
I love it. People is very friendly here.
Mistake alert. But don't worry. We will fix that one later. Back to the story. Frank smiles and says, "That's nice to hear. This is my dog, Peanut."
Oh, he's so cute! Hi, Peanut! Can I take a photo of him?
Sure. He loves the camera.
So I took a photo. Then another photo. Then ten more photos.
Ten photos of a dog. At seven thirty in the morning.
He was very cute, Leo! Then I said, "Have a good day, Frank!"
And Frank says, "You too, Mia. See you around." So, Mia, what did you do next?
I was hungry, and I needed coffee. A lot of coffee. So I walked to the coffee shop on my street.
Okay. Now I'll be the barista. Hi there! What can I get for you?
Hi! I'd like a medium latte, please.
Sure. Hot or iced?
Hot, please. It's cold this morning.
It sure is. Anything else?
Hmm. Yes. I'd like a blueberry muffin, too.
Good choice. They're fresh. Is that for here or to go?
To go, please. I'm a little late.
No problem. Can I get a name for the cup?
Mia. M, I, A.
Thanks, Mia. That's seven fifty. Your latte will be ready in two minutes.
Sounds good! Can I pay with my card?
Of course. Just tap it here.
So I paid, and I waited. And then the barista called my name. But he said, "Maya!"
A small mistake. It happens a lot with names.
I didn't care. The coffee was perfect. Then I looked at my phone, and I saw the time. Seven fifty-five!
And your new job starts at what time?
At eight thirty. And I didn't know the way to the office by bus. It was my first time taking the bus there.
Okay. So you needed directions.
Now I'll be a woman on the street. She is waiting at the corner.
Excuse me. Sorry to bother you. How do I get to Green Street?
Green Street? Hmm. It's a little far to walk. You can take the number twelve bus.
The number twelve. Okay. Where is the bus stop?
Go straight, and turn left at the bank. The bus stop is across from the pharmacy.
Go straight, and turn left at the bank. Across from the pharmacy. Thank you so much!
No problem. But hurry! The bus comes every fifteen minutes.
So I walked fast. I turned left at the bank, and I saw the bus stop. And I saw the number twelve bus. It was right there!
Great!
No, not great. Because then I saw a dog. A big, fluffy, white dog. And I stopped.
Let me guess. You took a photo.
Just one! Okay, maybe three. And when I looked up, the bus was leaving. Bye bye, bus.
Oh no.
So I waited for the next bus. Fifteen minutes. In the cold. With my coffee.
And then?
The next bus came. I got on and asked the driver, "Does this bus go to Green Street?"
I'll be the driver. Yes, it does. It's the fourth stop.
Great, thank you. And then I counted the stops. One, two, three, four. And I got off.
And what time did you get to work?
Eight forty-five. Fifteen minutes late. On my second week.
Well, now you know why Mia said, "I lost the bus." But we still won't tell you the right answer. Not yet.
Wait for it!
Okay. Let's stop the story for a moment. It's time for word focus. Five everyday expressions from Mia's morning.
Number one is from my neighbor, Frank.
How's it going?

card.significado: A friendly way to say "How are you?"

falas.texto: How's it going? It means, how are you? It's friendly and very common. You can answer, "Good, thanks!" or "Not bad." Here are two examples.
Hey, Sam! How's it going?
Hi, Mia! How's it going? Good to see you.
Now you. Say it with me. How's it going?
Number two. I said this to Frank, too.
I just moved here.

card.significado: I came to live here a short time ago.
card.exemplo: I just moved here, so I don't know the city.

falas.texto: I just moved here. Just means a short time ago. So, I came to live here very recently. Two examples.
I just moved here, so I don't know the city very well.
Welcome! Did you just move here from another country?
Say it with me. I just moved here.
Number three is from the coffee shop.
I'd like...

card.significado: A polite way to say what you want.
card.exemplo: I'd like a medium latte, please.

falas.texto: I'd like. It's short for I would like. It's a polite way to say what you want. Use it in shops, cafes, and restaurants. Two examples.
I'd like a medium latte, please.
I'd like a ticket to the city center, please.
Say it with me. I'd like a medium latte, please.

card.en: I'd like a medium latte, please.

falas.texto: Number four. I asked a woman on the street.
How do I get to...?

card.significado: A question to ask for directions to a place.
card.exemplo: Excuse me, how do I get to Green Street?

falas.texto: How do I get to? We use it to ask for directions. After to, say the place. Two examples.
Excuse me, how do I get to Green Street?
How do I get to the train station from here?
Say it with me. How do I get to the train station?

card.en: How do I get to the train station?

falas.texto: And number five. I said it to the barista.
Sounds good!

card.significado: Okay, I like that idea. I agree with that plan.

falas.texto: Sounds good. It means, okay, that's a good idea, or, I agree with that plan. Two examples.
Lunch at twelve thirty? Sounds good!
Let's meet at the park at ten. Sounds good!
Say it with me. Sounds good!
Great job. Five expressions. How's it going. I just moved here. I'd like. How do I get to. And sounds good. Listen for them in part two of the story.
Okay, so I got to the office. Fifteen minutes late. I was very nervous.
I'll be your coworker. What's his name?
His name is Sam. He sits next to me. He's really nice.
Okay. I'm Sam. Hey, Mia! How's it going?
Hi, Sam! Not great. I'm late. I'm so sorry.
Don't worry. The boss isn't here yet. She's on a call. Coffee?
No, thanks. I already have one. I'd like some water, though.
Sure. The water is in the kitchen. So, how do you like the city?
I like it a lot. But it's big. I just moved here, so I get lost a lot.
Ha. I did too, when I first moved here. Did you do anything fun last weekend?
Not really. On Saturday, I cleaned my new apartment. On Sunday, I went to a museum. And you?
I went hiking with my brother. It rained the whole time.
Oh no! Did you have fun?
We did, actually. We got very wet, but it was fun.
And then Sam asked me something important.
Hey, did the boss send you a message about the meeting?
Yes. She said me the meeting is at ten.
Mistake alert number two. We'll fix it later. Okay, Sam says, "Ten? Great. That gives us time. Do you want to get lunch together later?"
Sure! I'd love to. Where do people eat around here?
There's a good taco place across the street. Twelve thirty?
Sounds good!
And how was the meeting?
Long. Very long. But I understood almost everything. I was happy.
That's great, Mia. And after work?
After work, I went to the supermarket. My fridge was empty. Only one old lemon.
Okay. I'll be the cashier. Hi! Did you find everything okay?
Yes, thank you. Oh, wait. There's no price on these avocados. How much costs it?
Mistake alert number three. Last one, I promise. The cashier says, "Let me check. They're a dollar fifty each."
Okay. I'd like three, please.
Sure. Do you need a bag?
Yes, please. A paper bag, if you have one.
Here you go. Do you have our store card?
No, I don't. I just moved here.
No problem. You can get one online. It's free. Okay, your total is twenty-three dollars and forty cents.
Here you go. Can I pay with cash?
Of course. And here's your change. Have a good one!
You too! And then, when I walked out of the store, my phone rang. It was my friend Nora. She lives here, too.
Okay. I'll be Nora. Hey, Mia! How's it going? How was your day?
Hi, Nora! It was a busy day. A really busy day. I'll tell you everything later.
Ha. Okay. Listen, are you free on Saturday?
Saturday? Yes, I'm free. Why?
There's a big farmers market in the park. Do you want to go with me? We can get breakfast there.
I'd love to! What time?
Let's meet at nine thirty. At the main gate of the park.
Nine thirty. Okay. But wait. How do I get to the park from my apartment?
Take the number twelve bus. Get off at the fifth stop. The gate is right there.
The number twelve bus. Again! Okay. Sounds good!
And Mia, please. Don't stop for any dogs this time.
Ha ha. How do you know about the dogs?
I know you, Mia. See you Saturday!
See you Saturday, Nora! And then I went home, and I called you, Leo.
And here we are. What a day. Okay, Mia. You made a few mistakes today. Let's fix them.
Welcome to my favorite part. Mistake fix. Three mistakes from Mia's day. Don't worry, Mia. Everybody makes these.
Okay. I'm ready. Be nice.
Always. Mistake number one. Mia said to her neighbor, "People is very friendly here."
What's wrong with that?
People is a plural word. It means more than one person. So we say people are, not people is. People are very friendly here.
People are very friendly here. Oh, like, the people are nice, the people are busy.
Exactly. One person is. Two or more people are. Say it with me. People are very friendly here.
Mistake number two. Mia said to Sam, "She said me the meeting is at ten."

card.errado: She said me the meeting is at ten.
card.certo: She told me the meeting is at ten.

falas.texto: Hmm. Is it told?
Yes! Here is the simple rule. Tell, then a person. Told me. Told Sam. Told her. But never say, then a person. She said the meeting is at ten.
So, she told me the meeting is at ten. Or, she said the meeting is at ten.
Perfect. Both are correct. Just don't say, she said me. Say it with me. She told me the meeting is at ten.
Mistake number three. At the supermarket, Mia asked, "How much costs it?"
I know, I know. In my language, it sounds okay.
It does in many languages. But in English, questions often need do or does. So we say, how much does it cost? Or the easy way. How much is it?
How much does it cost? How much is it? And for avocados, it's more than one. So, how much are they?
Wow. That's a great point, Mia. How much are they? Yes. Say it with me. How much does it cost?
So, three mistakes. People are. She told me. And how much does it cost. Fixed!
Mistakes fixed!

And now, the quiz. At the start, Mia said, "This morning, I lost the bus." What should she say?
I know it now. I thought about it all day.
Go on, then.
This morning, I missed the bus.

card.texto: This morning, I missed the bus.

falas.texto: Correct! You miss a bus, a train, or a plane. That means you are too late, and it goes without you. You lose things like your keys or your phone. That means you can't find them.
So, I missed the bus, but I didn't lose my phone. Because I was using it to take photos of a dog.
Exactly. I missed the bus. I lost my keys. Say it with me. This morning, I missed the bus.
Let's do a quick recap of today.
